note: Resource-based policy approach lets the instance keep its own role for both the read and the write.
D also works for S3 but does not cover the 'several other actions' and one-place management in the production account.
Assumes the allow-list default model: with FullAWSAccess detached, an Allow must exist at every level on the path.
Assumes 'see drift' maps to detective controls and 'standard configuration' to Account Factory.
SCPs do not apply to the management account; the Production OU members are assumed to be member accounts.
OAI does not support SSE-KMS; OAC does.
OAC does not work with S3 website endpoints; use the REST endpoint.
No option mentions HTTPS (origin protocol policy), so I chose by elimination. A (bucket owner enforced) is the weakest of the three; the stem does not say why it is required.
Wording 'Add MFA protection to the role' is vague; the real mechanism is an aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition in the role trust policy. C is the only sensible option.
Cross-account needs allow on both sides: resource policy (PrincipalOrgID) and identity policy in the caller.
